query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractStrong static magnetic field (SSMF) is a unique way to regulate the microstructure and improve the properties of materials. FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy is a novel class of soft magnetic materials (SMMs) designed based on high-entropy alloy (HEA) concepts. In this study, a strong static magnetic field is introduced to tune the microstructure, mechanical, electrical and magnetic properties of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 high-entropy alloy. Results indicate that, with the increasing magnetic field intensity, the Vickers hardness and the saturation magnetization (Ms) increase firstly, and then decrease and reach the maximum at 5T, while the yield strength, the residual magnetization (Mr) and the coercivity (Hc) take the opposite trend. The resistivity values (ρ) are found to be enhanced by the increasing magnetic field intensity. The main reasons for the magnetic field on the above effects are interpreted by microstructure evolution (phase species and volume fraction), atomic-level structure and defects (vacancy and dislocation density).Keywords: strong static magnetic field, high-entropy alloy, solidification, microstructure evolution, comprehensive properties

The effect of SSMF on the microstructure during solidification is bound to the properties of the material after solidification, such as mechanical properties [], thermoelectric properties [,] and magnetic properties [,]. In the existing literature reports, the role of strong magnetic field in the solidification process focuses on pure metal [,], binary alloy system [,,,] and ternary alloy system [,,,,]. Few articles have the application of SSMF during the solidification of HEAs. FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy is a novel class of soft magnetic materials (SMMs) based on HEAs. SMMs require high Ms, high ρ, low Hc and low Mr, in addition to good malleability []. Zhang et al. studied the effects of composition changes on microstructure and mechanical, electrical as well as magnetic properties of FeCoNi(AlSi)x HEA [] Zuo et al. found that the microstructures and magnetic behaviors of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 HEA were affected by the Bridgman solidification []. In this report, SSMF is introduced during the solidification process of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 HEA, and its effect on the microstructure evolution and properties are studied.

cited_evidence.text: where Hc is the coercivity, D the grain size, Ms the magnetization saturation, K1 the magneto-crystalline anisotropy, KB the Boltzmann constant, Tc the Curie temperature, and α the lattice constant. When the grain size is almost the same, the change trend of Hc may be related to Ms and K1 from this equation. When Ms reaches the maximum, the coercivity has the minimum value. In addition, the abnormal change of magnetic properties (Ms, Hc and Mr) at 7T may be related to the precipitated BCC phase. In the SMMs, high Ms, low Hc and low Mr are excellent results for use. In short, the magnetic behaviors of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 HEA are improved by the solidification under the magnetic field, and the soft magnetic properties of the alloy are further optimized.

In this study, the microstructure evolution and properties of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 HEA solidified under SSMF have been systematically investigated. We find that the solidification technology under magnetic field can be used to improve the soft magnetic properties of the alloy. The main conclusions are as follows: During the solidification of different magnetic field intensities, the alloy solidified up to 5T is still a single FCC phase, and has the maximum Vickers hardness values (190 HV and 187 HV in the parallel and perpendicular direction of the magnetic field, respectively) and the minimum yield strength value (172 MPa). The electrical resistivity increases with the magnetic field intensity, and the maximum value is 110 μΩ·cm at 7T. The maximum saturation magnetization values of the vertical and parallel magnetic field direction are 121.7 emu/g and 97.7 emu/g at 5T. The minimum coercivity values are 2.19 Oe and 2.29 Oe at 5T, respectively.

decision.rationale: Direction A directly addresses the limitation of low coercive field in single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys by introducing a strong static magnetic field during solidification. The critic's review suggests that this direction is viable with changes, and the proposed fix is to investigate the effect of the magnetic field on the microstructure and properties of the alloy in more detail. This direction has supporting evidence from the eligible evidence records, including PMC7512793, which demonstrates the improvement of soft magnetic properties of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy under a strong static magnetic field.
